title: Instant Pot Chicken Pepper Rasam
equip: Instant Pot (pressure cook + sauté), small deep nonstick pan (tadka), mortar and pestle

items.n: tamarind, soaked in 250 ml hot water

steps.x: Rub the skinned thighs with 3 g salt and 1 g turmeric. Leave for 10 min while you do the next two steps.
Soak the tamarind in 250 ml hot water for 10 min. Squeeze it out with your fingers, strain, and discard the pulp. Quarter the tomatoes.
In the mortar, coarsely crush 1.2 g pepper, the cumin, the coriander seeds and the garlic. Keep it coarse for texture, not a paste.

Add to the Instant Pot: thighs, tomatoes, tamarind water, 750 ml water, 6 g salt, 1 g turmeric and the crushed base spices. Seal and cook on High pressure for 12 min. Natural release for 10 min, then quick release.

Lift the thighs out onto a plate. Mash the tomatoes against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle. Don't use the hand blender, as it clouds the rasam. Pull the meat off the bones in bite-size chunks and discard the bones. Return about three-quarters of the meat to the pot.
Before any adult pepper goes in, ladle about 250 ml of broth with the reserved chicken into a bowl.
Press Sauté. Add the 2.5 g freshly crushed pepper and the naatu sakkarai to the pot. Simmer gently for 5 min. Don't hard boil, or the pepper turns bitter. Taste and add salt if needed.

Heat the ghee in the small nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and wait until they pop. Add the hing and curry leaves for 5 seconds. Pour half into the child's bowl. Add the dried chillies to the pan for 10 seconds, then pour into the pot.
Turn off Sauté. Stir in the coriander. Rest with the lid on for 5 min, then serve over hot rice.

notes: Meant to be thin. If it tastes too sharp, add 100 ml hot water and 2 g more naatu sakkarai.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 2 months frozen. Reheat gently and never boil hard.
Meal prep: portion chicken and rasam together, and add the coriander after reheating.
Keep the skin off. It makes the rasam greasy and muddy.
source: None. Adapted from the standard Tamil pepper rasam method.
